Done

This behavior was somewhat on purpose.  A default constructed object_path basically shouldn't be used, but was required in the context of unpacking.

Do you have an example of where this would be used in code?

> A default constructed object_path basically shouldn't be used

Well, it is used multiple times in bmcweb
```
 rg -i "sdbusplus::message::object_path .*Path;"
features/openbmc_rest/image_upload.hpp
81:            sdbusplus::message::object_path path;

redfish-core/src/dbus_log_watcher.cpp
79:    sdbusplus::message::object_path objectPath;

redfish-core/include/utils/systems_utils.hpp
151:    sdbusplus::message::object_path systemPath;

redfish-core/lib/update_service.hpp
272:    sdbusplus::message::object_path objPath;
421:    sdbusplus::message::object_path objPath;

redfish-core/lib/certificate_service.hpp
573:    sdbusplus::message::object_path objectPath;
891:            sdbusplus::message::object_path csrObjectPath;
```

> but was required in the context of unpacking.

But that's what friend classes/methods are for, right? 

Currently that intent of "shouldn't be used" does not look like it's even documented.

Anyways, can you explain why it is required for unpacking? I'm not completely following why it can't be done some other way.

There's also a number of cases where the root path is explicitly constructed.
```
redfish-core/lib/hypervisor_system.hpp
331:    sdbusplus::message::object_path path("/");
redfish-core/lib/sensors.hpp
1190:    sdbusplus::message::object_path path("/");
```

In both cases, default-constructing with `"/"` would be either safer or less verbose (but in unpacking cases, create some extra overhead).


For the unpacking use-case, could it be more appropriate to directly create the correct object path instead of creating an invalid one and then modifying it at some later point? That robs us of the ability to make it `const`, creating readability problems in bmcweb code (mutable object path which is never modified after unpacking).

> Do you have an example of where this would be used in code?

Yes, you can have a look at reactors with generated servers. Rarely they will have interfaces which have a property of type object path. If the default constructor is wrong for object path is wrong then these will throw unless the properties are initialized.

That makes using the (a)server unnecessarily bug prone and *inconsistent* (some interfaces can default-construct, others cannot).

> > A default constructed object_path basically shouldn't be used
> 
> Well, it is used multiple times in bmcweb
> ```
>  rg -i "sdbusplus::message::object_path .*Path;"
> features/openbmc_rest/image_upload.hpp
> 81:            sdbusplus::message::object_path path;
> 
> redfish-core/src/dbus_log_watcher.cpp
> 79:    sdbusplus::message::object_path objectPath;
> 
> redfish-core/include/utils/systems_utils.hpp
> 151:    sdbusplus::message::object_path systemPath;
> 
> redfish-core/lib/update_service.hpp
> 272:    sdbusplus::message::object_path objPath;
> 421:    sdbusplus::message::object_path objPath;
> 
> redfish-core/lib/certificate_service.hpp
> 573:    sdbusplus::message::object_path objectPath;
> 891:            sdbusplus::message::object_path csrObjectPath;
> ```
> 
> > but was required in the context of unpacking.
> 
> But that's what friend classes/methods are for, right? 
> 
> Currently that intent of "shouldn't be used" does not look like it's even documented.
> 
> Anyways, can you explain why it is required for unpacking? I'm not completely following why it can't be done some other way.

You found a couple of examples in bmcweb of why, lets take your first one in your list:
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/8f04d1710bb90a9dd225ce9b82cb0c157460b4a4/features/openbmc_rest/image_upload.hpp#L81

You'll note you have to default construct the object_path so that you can pass it to the read(...) call.  If you use that path object without having called a successful read() on it, the object is invalid.

> 
> There's also a number of cases where the root path is explicitly constructed.
> ```
> redfish-core/lib/hypervisor_system.hpp
> 331:    sdbusplus::message::object_path path("/");
> redfish-core/lib/sensors.hpp
> 1190:    sdbusplus::message::object_path path("/");
> ```
> 
> In both cases, default-constructing with `"/"` would be either safer or less verbose (but in unpacking cases, create some extra overhead).

I actually prefer the verbosity there.  It makes it VERY clear at the call site what path is being put in. FWIW, the hypervisor_system.hpp example is something we wouldn't even recommend anymore.  Generally we put object managers on a namespace, not the root, but that code is old and hasn't kept up with best practices.

The code in sensors.hpp is actually an antipattern now that the mapper has association calls, but that code you're pointing to has existed for 7 years.
But that's kind of the point, there's no correct usage off the top of my head where you should be relying on a default constructed path of "/", so making it the default isn't great.

> 
> 
> For the unpacking use-case, could it be more appropriate to directly create the correct object path instead of creating an invalid one and then modifying it at some later point? That robs us of the ability to make it `const`, creating readability problems in bmcweb code (mutable object path which is never modified after unpacking).

I don't understand what you're suggesting about const here.  FWIW, for new usage, Patrick put in the unpack<> methods which in theory don't require default construction (or could use friend classes like you suggest).  IF we're going to refactor, I'd rather we continue pushing those out rather than try to make object_path default construct.

> 
> > Do you have an example of where this would be used in code?
> 
> Yes, you can have a look at reactors with generated servers. Rarely they will have interfaces which have a property of type object path. If the default constructor is wrong for object path is wrong then these will throw unless the properties are initialized.

I'm not seeing it, can you give me a pointer to the code you're talking about?  I would expect every property to be explicitly initialized to something sane for that interface, not relying on the underlying object_path object to do something reasonable.

> 
> That makes using the (a)server unnecessarily bug prone and *inconsistent* (some interfaces can default-construct, others cannot).

I think we can solve this net-issue in a different way.  Ideally the above should be in your commit message describing why this change should go through.

From my perspective, I would rather we prioritize getting everything using the unpack() calls, and deprecate the default constructor entirely rather than try to improve it.  FWIW, I can't really think of a case where a property pointing at "/" is correct behavior either, so in that case we've moved from a startup bug to a runtime bug?

> I would expect every property to be explicitly initialized to something
 sane for that interface, not relying on the underlying object_path 
object to do something reasonable.

There is a constructor for generated server which does not take properties. If you were right, we would not have that constructor?

Independently of the developer, IMO sdbusplus needs to make a best effort to not break D-Bus by creating invalid values for object path.

> FWIW, I can't really think of a case where a property pointing at "/" is
 correct behavior either

`/` could be used to indicate absence of a value, so there is a use-case for it. 
Using special values to represent optional is widely used in the PDI.
It depends on the interface and what it needs to represent.

> so in that case we've moved from a startup bug
 to a runtime bug?

D-Bus interfaces are not only created at startup, they can be created at any point in time. IMO it is preferable to not throw and terminate as a default behavior.

> and deprecate the default constructor entirely rather than try to improve it.  

That idea creates lots of edge cases in the mako cpp and python code for the generated headers.

I estimate it would be a large amount of work to implement your idea since then default construction of some interfaces via generated server will not be possible anymore. The generated code and the code to generate it is already quite complicated so i would try to avoid going down that route.

> > I would expect every property to be explicitly initialized to something
>  sane for that interface, not relying on the underlying object_path 
> object to do something reasonable.
> 
> There is a constructor for generated server which does not take properties. If you were right, we would not have that constructor?

This is object path, not properties, but yes, I would expect every object path to be set at some point, and not rely on a default.

> 
> Independently of the developer, IMO sdbusplus needs to make a best effort to not break D-Bus by creating invalid values for object path.

I agree with the statement, I disagree that it should promote incorrect code to do it.  If you default initialize an object_path, then use it, you're doing something wrong.  Maybe we default it to /this/object_path/is/wrong?  (That's not a serious suggestion)

> 
> > FWIW, I can't really think of a case where a property pointing at "/" is
>  correct behavior either
> 
> `/` could be used to indicate absence of a value, so there is a use-case for it. 

Empty string currently indicates the absence of a value.  I'm not sure why we'd rely on a valid path as "absence".

> Using special values to represent optional is widely used in the PDI.
> It depends on the interface and what it needs to represent.
> 
> > so in that case we've moved from a startup bug
>  to a runtime bug?
> 
> D-Bus interfaces are not only created at startup, they can be created at any point in time. IMO it is preferable to not throw and terminate as a default behavior.

We agree in this.  Where do we terminate if an object_path is unset?  That should be making sure that if an incorrect object path is used it doesn't terminate.

> 
> > and deprecate the default constructor entirely rather than try to improve it.  
> 
> That idea creates lots of edge cases in the mako cpp and python code for the generated headers.
> 
> I estimate it would be a large amount of work to implement your idea since then default construction of some interfaces via generated server will not be possible anymore. The generated code and the code to generate it is already quite complicated so i would try to avoid going down that route.

I don't know if we agree in those estimates, but without patches we're both guessing.  Hence why the default constructor exists as it is.  It is very obvious when you have a bug at startup.  If we accept this patch, now we silently get a path of /, which is almost always incorrect.  I'd rather we keep the incorrect behavior return an error rather than silently doing "something".

aserver is all generated code, and worked before this patch, so clearly wasn't using this codepath.

I looked through 287 files where object_path is used to check all the places where we might be default-initializing an object path and resulting in incorrect behavior if we were to change the default-default.

```
$ rg "object_path[^=&]+" -l -t cpp | grep -v systemd | grep -v ipmitool | grep -v libgpiod | grep -v test | wc
    287     287   12704
```

There is exactly one case that gives me any concern and I think that is a bug in that there is a dbus method call that isn't returning an error.

phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/bmc/update_manager.cpp : startUpdate method

> If you default initialize an object_path, then use it, you're doing something wrong. Maybe we default it to /this/object_path/is/wrong? (That's not a serious suggestion)

@ed@tanous.net

Why must this be true?  I don't see anything intrinsically wrong with having the default become "/" (the root).

> Empty string currently indicates the absence of a value. I'm not sure why we'd rely on a valid path as "absence".

When is an "absent object_path" necessary?  I'm not finding any code paths that rely on this conceptually.

> So a small mistake in initializing an interface can bring down an entire application because of the exception.

@alexander.hansen@9elements.com

We can alternatively fix the generated code to ensure it never sends out a bogus object_path, right?  Thankfully it seems like dbus itself is preventing us from sending a bogus object_path but we should probably be better at that in the bindings.

> This patch is not specific to "startup".

No disagreement.

> So a small mistake in initializing an interface can bring down an entire application because of the exception.

Only if there's a failure to catch the resulting exception?  That seems more a reason to not use exceptions for this case, or to make sure that that exceptions are caught.  Simply making this a silent error I don't think is the answer.

> I looked through 287 files 

I agree, this patchset itself is unlikely to directly break anything.  I'm worried about future regressions where object_path is now default constructable with a path that isn't obviously incorrect as Alexander gives in his example.  That example would compile and run, but is now silently incorrect because there's no correct daemon that directly adds objects at the root anymore.

> I don't see anything intrinsically wrong with having the default become "/"

Based on our naming conventions for namespaces, I can't think of any correct usage where / would be a correct path?  Maybe I'm missing something?

> When is an "absent object_path" necessary?

The only reason I did it in the first place is because to read a property you used to have to do
object_path path;
obj.read(path);

Which required having some default constructor.  unpack I think fixes this use, in which case I think we make the default constructor private once we've moved to unpack everywhere

> We can alternatively fix the generated code to ensure it never sends out a bogus object_path, right?

This would be my mid-strong preference to avoid footguns in default constructing an objects and forgetting to declare a path.



@alexander, was there a real piece of code that had a default initialized bug that drove this, or was this just wanting to use object_path in more places?  The example you gave wouldn't pick / as the object path in a real application, so it confuses me a little.

> I agree, this patchset itself is unlikely to directly break anything.  
I'm worried about future regressions where object_path is now default 
constructable with a path that isn't obviously incorrect as Alexander 
gives in his example.  That example would compile and run, but is now 
silently incorrect because there's no correct daemon that directly adds 
objects at the root anymore.

So the application may have crashed, and with this patch it (or its clients) does not crash anymore. Is that a regression to you?

Note that a single application may expose various object paths under various namespaces. IMO a failure to initialize an object path properly should not have a blast radius larger than necessary.

>  but is now silently incorrect

How did you come to this conclusion? Usually applications provide a highly visible `lg2::error` message if they encounter unexpected / missing values / object paths on D-Bus and still continue with other tasks instead of crashing.

> > We can alternatively fix the generated code to ensure it never sends out a bogus object_path, right?

> This would be my mid-strong preference to avoid footguns in default constructing an objects and forgetting to declare a path.

That's just a partial fix and on top of that it's conceptually inconsistent. Why should an object path as part of a generated server produce a different default value than when it's constructed independently?

The default constructor is wrong so it should be fixed or go away. The problem is not just in the generated code.
If we accept this `""` as our internal state then technically every function receiving an object path would need do object path validation. It's like needing to check `int*` for `nullptr`.

> @alexander, was there a real piece of code that had a default 
initialized bug that drove this, or was this just wanting to use 
object_path in more places?

I hit this bug sometimes but i do not remember the specific patch. Since i tested my code i changed over to pass the properties to initialize the interface.

So yes, it's a real bug that people can hit and unnecessarily error prone API in combination with the generated server.

The application would only crash if you failed to catch the exceptions thrown.  Functionally, the application still doesn't work if it's relying on a default constructed dbus path.

>

Agreed, but if you're using exceptions, that relies on catching that exception and handling it rather than just making the code do something you didn't intend but "allowed"

I'm not sure what you mean.  How is "A user should always set an object path." inconsistent?

>

Agreed, so lets make it go away, not be relied on more.  This change will allow more code that's incorrect to "just work", even though it's silently wrong.

> If we accept this `""` as our internal state then technically every function receiving an object path would need do object path validation. It's like needing to check `int*` for `nullptr`.

I would say it's different than checking for nullptr, (in that case we would say use string_view to avoid that problem), but yes, functions do check for bad dbus paths already, that's where the exception was being thrown, no?

> initialized bug that drove this, or was this just wanting to use 
> object_path in more places?
>

That's what I would expect correct code to do, that's why I don't want this patch, it's an API that makes people believe their code works.

>

No example was provided of correct code that hit that bug, so I'm confused.  Yes, you can hit that path from incorrect code, but if we're trying to make the API easier to use, removing the default constructor entirely seems preferable.

### currently it's broken and needs to be fixed

> but if we're trying to make the API easier to use, removing the default constructor entirely seems preferable.

Core guideline
https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#c43-ensure-that-a-copyable-class-has-a-default-constructor
 applies here. The exemption

> Classes that don’t have a reasonable default construction are usually 
not copyable either, so they don’t fall under this guideline.

does not apply since `/` is both valid and reasonable as a default value for an object path.

> Empty string currently indicates the absence of a value.  

Also https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#c42-if-a-constructor-cannot-construct-a-valid-object-throw-an-exception
and https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#c41-a-constructor-should-create-a-fully-initialized-object

D-Bus API Design guidelines  https://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-api-design.html also has something to say under the **API versioning** section.

> Note, however, that supporting multiple interface versions simultaneously
  requires that object paths are versioned as well, so objects must not
  be put on the bus at the root path (‘/’). 

I think the key point is that `sdbusplus::message::object_path` is a value wrapper for a D-Bus object-path value, not a policy type for “recommended exported OpenBMC object locations”.

Currently the `string_path_wrapper::parent_path()` is also wrong because it returns `"/"` as the parent path of `""` (the current default value).

**An empty string has no parent path because it's not even a path.**

The `parent_path` of the default value should probably be the default value again, that's in line with
https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/filesystem/path/parent_path.html
and what linux does.

### possibility of a stricter object path (without `/`)

If you are interested in a class to represent object paths excluding `/`, that should probably be modeled separately. 

Let's explore what would be required for `sdbusplus::message::obj_path` (strict).

First of all the `parent_path` implementation for such a class is different since
`sdbusplus::message::obj_path("/xyz")` is `/` which is of the regular `object_path` type. 
So we can only return that there. Which already tells us that we need the regular `object_path` type in addition to that stricter type.

`sdbusplus::message::obj_path` has no meaningful default construction but can be copied. When constructing `sdbusplus::message::obj_path`, validation can be used to make sure we have at least one path segment.

One benefit is that the `sdbusplus::message::obj_path::filename()` function will always return a non-empty string since we have at least one path segment.

To summarize, a stricter version of object path seems possible from a first look, but a wider object path implementation (allowing `/`) is still necessary to form a **complete** API.

> ### currently it's broken and needs to be fixed

We disagree, and repeated asks for examples of correct code that's broken have been ignored.

> 
> > but if we're trying to make the API easier to use, removing the default constructor entirely seems preferable.
> 
> Core guideline
> https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#c43-ensure-that-a-copyable-class-has-a-default-constructor

We implement this today without this patch, there's no requirement that the default-constructed state is usable as-is.

> 
> > Classes that don’t have a reasonable default construction are usually 
> not copyable either, so they don’t fall under this guideline.
> 
> does not apply since `/` is both valid and reasonable as a default value for an object path.

This is where we disagree. "/" is not a reasonable default.  There is no service that is correctly publishing at /.  Anything that was has been moved to the appropriate namespace.

> 
> > Empty string currently indicates the absence of a value.  
> 
> Also https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#c42-if-a-constructor-cannot-construct-a-valid-object-throw-an-exception

So we should throw an exception on a default construction?

> and https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#c41-a-constructor-should-create-a-fully-initialized-object

Right, this is why we should remove the default constructor.

Throughout this conversation we talked about 3 different classes

- S1: maybe-contains-an-object-path (e.g. ``, ` `, `foo`, `bar`, `/`, `//` `/xyz/`)
- S2: actually-contains-an-object-path (e.g.(`/`, `/xyz`, `/com/ibm`)

If you model that as sets, you get
```
S1 contains S2 
S2 contains S3
```

It looks like you are trying to make `sdbusplus::message::object_path` behave as S1 and S3 which is not possible in terms of API design.

If it's S3 then it automatically is S2 which requires the D-Bus object path invariant.

IMO, from the perspective of sdbusplus, the actually-contains-an-object-path value type is the only thing that makes sense to use internally since sdbusplus is a D-Bus abstraction and not tied to `/xyz` object path namespace.

It needs to be able to represent every object path.

If you need some type in user code that always contains a non-root object path, you need to use a different class, not `sdbusplus::message::object_path`.
